## 2. LLM calls per successful analytics question: 2

| | call 1 - interpreter | call 2 - explainer |
|---|---|---|
| input | fixed instructions + minimal context (reference date, first/last sale date, optional-field flags) + the question | the question + the verified FACT sentences + notes + up to 10 verified table rows |
| output | JSON, strictly validated into `Interpretation` (unknown fields rejected) | JSON `{interpretation, suggestion}`; each part kept only if it passes the number/causal/markup guards |
| rows visible | no | only the verified result rows (<= 10) |
| ground truth visible | **no** | no pandas ground truth; it does see the engine's verified facts, by design |
| other tenants' data visible | no | no |
| max_tokens / temperature | 700 / 0 | 300 / 0 |
| timeout / retries | `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30 s) per attempt; tenacity 9.0.0: up to 3 attempts, backoff 0.5-4 s, on transport errors and HTTP errors (4xx included); latency includes retries | same |
| failure behaviour | any failure/invalid output -> legacy router, flagged `path=legacy_router`, category recorded | answer keeps the deterministic FACT text (`explanation_source=template`) |
| measurement | per-call latency (retries included), attempts, provider-reported tokens, echoed model id (recorder + audit) | same |

## 3. Ground-truth isolation

* Whitelist check of the exact interpreter request for all 27 frozen questions: **0 violations**; 41 ground-truth numeric fragments scanned; baseline code-prompt collisions: 0.
* The runner installs the same check as a fail-closed guard in front of every provider call (a violating request is never sent and aborts the run); the mock run recorded `{"guard": "whitelist check of every interpreter request + ground-truth fragment scan; a violating request is never sent and aborts the run", "forbidden_fragment_count": 41}` and no violation.
* Interpreter receives: fixed interpreter instructions; reference date; first/last recorded sale date; which optional fields exist (booleans); the frozen question text.
* Interpreter does not receive: expected answer; pandas ground truth; score or tolerance; task id; any sales row; product names; other tenants' data.
* The engine runs only after the interpretation; the explainer receives the verified facts because explaining them is its job.

## 7. Task split and unsupported track

115 primary attempts (23 tasks x 5 repeats) go through the analytics path; 20 GST attempts: 20 refused as unsupported, 0 counted in accuracy. GST refusals are neither model failures nor successes (outcome `unsupported_by_design`, excluded from agreement rates).

## 8. Baseline

**Reference tool-use system: NOT a simpler baseline, NOT DecisionGPT.** the same LLMClient + a sandboxed pandas tool over the same evaluation view (protocol B2): code-writing call, sandbox execution (<=1 repair), phrasing call. Fair as a reference: True; silently redesigned: False. Documented asymmetries:
* it is MORE expressive than DecisionGPT (arbitrary pandas vs a closed request vocabulary), so it is a capability reference, not a handicapped control
* it is shown column descriptions, the first 5 rows and the date range; the DecisionGPT interpreter is shown no rows and no product names
* its numbers come from code the model writes; DecisionGPT's come from a fixed engine - so it measures the model's code, not its arithmetic
* it receives the gst_pct column on the 4 GST tasks only (DecisionGPT cannot: the production schema has no GST field)
* its phrasing step has no number guard
* it reads the view DataFrame directly, not through production ingestion, authentication or tenant scoping
Must not be called: LLM-only baseline, simpler baseline, human baseline, a competing DecisionGPT system.
